answer: Sybils stay cheap when a new name can trade at full size on day one. Auction a weekly allotment of onyx permits instead: each binds to one key and cannot be reassigned. Holders may clear contracts in a reserved oasis of high-value flow; others face small, delayed transfers. To keep a permit, the holder appends a counterparties log to a cedar archive that never rewrites history. If several keys share a funder, a device, or nearly the same log, attestors revoke those permits as one cluster and burn the deposits. A fake-identity swarm must then win many scarce permits and keep uncorrelated books.
